description: Checks whether an AI agent can read one website. Returns one flat row of 42 fields across five families: llms.txt (with llms-full.txt and ai.txt), robots.txt AI crawler policy including Content Signal directives, structured data (JSON-LD, microdata, Open Graph, canonical), render mode, and machine readable endpoints (sitemap, OpenAPI, well known files, feeds). Every field is read off a fetch and no model is called, so a repeat audit changes only when the site changes. Twelve requests per domain, typically 2 to 4 seconds. Use it to audit a site before and after AI crawler work, one domain per call. Do not use it to find which AI vendors a company pays for (that is the AI Tooling Detector) or to read page content. Requires an APIFY_TOKEN and consumes Apify credits: charged per domain analyzed plus a small run start fee. Read only.

check_endpoints.description: Alias for the checks array: false removes sitemap, openapi, security_txt and feeds. Ignored when checks is set. Default: true.

check_structured_data.description: Alias for the checks array: false removes json_ld, microdata, open_graph and canonical. Ignored when checks is set. Default: true.

checks.description: Run only these checks. Omit for all of them. Narrowing narrows the work as well as the answer: an llms_txt only audit makes three requests instead of ten. A check you did not run reports null, never false. The score is rescaled over the checks you selected, so a site with a perfect llms.txt audited for llms.txt alone reads 100 rather than 25.

domain.description: One company domain, for example vercel.com. A full URL is accepted: the protocol and path are stripped and the root of the domain is audited. One domain per call.

skipCache.description: Leave as false to use the 7 day cache. Set to true to re-audit the domain from scratch. Default: "false".

name: audit_agent_accessibility
title: Audit Agent Accessibility
